expected_prisoner.name: Johnny Baranski
expected_prisoner.description: Johnny Baranski was a haiku poet and Catholic Worker activist. His resistance to war and nuclear weapons led to several imprisonments, during which he wrote prison poetry.
expected_prisoner.body:
Historical photograph source

Portrait of poet and Catholic Worker peace activist Johnny Baranski; added by Kaypeg on February 4, 2018. Find a Grave photograph 165928949.

Separate Vancouver White Train case

The published primary opinion in State v. Aver, 109 Wn.2d 303 (November 5, 1987), names Johnny Wayne Baranski among the petitioners and affirms their train-obstruction convictions under RCW 81.48.020. Its facts identify Vancouver arrests by city police at a White Train protest, prosecuted in Clark County. This is distinct from the later Snohomish County jail stay. Primary opinion; Published opinion with full petitioner list.

The Berkeley-held Peace Law index, entry PL-33/28.6, identifies Washington v. Johnny Baranski and dates the White Train arrests July 24, 1984; it reports September convictions and differing fines. The exact arrest is recorded as a separate case. The available indexed passage was read, but the original PDF returned an access denial and was not visually verified. No individual fine, jail admission, release or time served is inferred. Peace Law index, PL-33/28.6.

The appellate decision date is not a new arrest or a release. Existing 1987 year-precision imprisonment remains unchanged; the sixty-day sentence does not establish an exact discharge day or a complete actual-custody total. His identified portrait and earlier cases are retained.

expected_cases.sentence: One-year federal sentence imposed in 1974; imprisonment at McNeil Island is documented. Exact custody endpoints and full time served are unverified.

expected_cases.charges: Anti-nuclear protest at the Trident base; individual statutory charge unverified
expected_cases.sentence: Six-month sentence following the 1979 Bangor Trident-base arrest. Actual imprisonment and prison writing at Lompoc are documented; exact custody endpoints remain unverified.

expected_cases.charges: Blocking a train carrying nuclear-weapons material; individual statutory charge unverified
expected_cases.sentence: Sixty-day sentence in 1987 for a railway blockade connected with the Trident base. His Snohomish County Jail poetry documents the imprisonment; exact endpoints remain unverified.

expected_cases.charges: Obstructing a train under RCW 81.48.020 — July 24, 1984 Vancouver White Train protest
expected_cases.convicted: Yes — conviction affirmed in State v. Aver (1987)
expected_cases.sentence: Separate Clark County train-obstruction prosecution. The Peace Law index reports September 1984 convictions and differing fines, without an individual fine amount or actual custody endpoints. Not the later 1987 Snohomish County sixty-day jail sentence.

case.charges: Refusal to pay a fine imposed for attempting to stop the nuclear-weapons train entering Bangor submarine base on March 22, 1983; individual statutory charge unverified.
case.sentence: Ordered to jail August 12, 1983 for eight days after refusing a $200 fine, credited at $25 per day. Contemporary report explicitly confirms August 20 release; subsequent issue includes his account of the eight days served. Initial March arrest is not treated as continuous custody. Sources: https://media.nukeresister.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/NR019_19830823small.pdf#page=6 ; https://media.nukeresister.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/NR020_19830930small.pdf#page=5

expected.charges: Criminal mischief, culpable negligence, trespass, resisting arrest without violence, and unlawful assembly: GE Three anti-nuclear protest, Largo, Florida.
expected.convicted: Convicted May 18, 1983 following a three-day jury trial on eighteen misdemeanor counts.
expected.sentence: Concurrent six-month and one-year sentences reported at May 26, 1983 sentencing. Released on bond between conviction and sentencing; returned to jail after sentencing without posting appeal bond. Actual release confirmed in 1983, exact day and month unresolved. January 1 is a year-only storage placeholder. Arrest month October 1982: contemporary report gives October 27 while the University of Florida archival account quotes October 14; neither day is asserted. Nominal sentence is not actual time served. Sources: https://media.nukeresister.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/NR017_19830606small.pdf#page=4 ; https://media.nukeresister.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/NR021_19831115small.pdf#page=3 ; https://pkyonge.uflib.ufl.edu/2022/07/20/the-florida-peace-movement-collection/

updates.sentence: Concurrent six-month and one-year sentences reported at May 26, 1983 sentencing. Released on bond between conviction and sentencing; returned to jail after sentencing without posting appeal bond. Actual release confirmed in 1983, exact day and month unresolved. January 1 is a year-only storage placeholder. Arrest month October 1982: contemporary report gives October 27 while the University of Florida archival account quotes October 14; neither day is asserted. Nominal sentence is not actual time served. Sources: https://media.nukeresister.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/NR017_19830606small.pdf#page=4 ; https://media.nukeresister.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/NR021_19831115small.pdf#page=3 ; https://pkyonge.uflib.ufl.edu/2022/07/20/the-florida-peace-movement-collection/ Subsequent contemporary follow-up reports rejection of an offered ninety days with probation and fine, followed by reduction of the original year term to 363 days by Judge Philip Federico. This is the imposed sentence, not an actual time-served total. Follow-up: https://media.nukeresister.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/NR019_19830823small.pdf#page=6
